name: Speculation
description: Speculation is a historical gambling game popular in the 18th and 19th centuries, famously depicted in Jane Austen's novels. The game revolves around players buying and selling the right to the 'Highest Trump' currently revealed. It is not trick-taking but a game of chance and negotiation, where the winner is the holder of the highest trump when all cards are revealed.

overview.description: Speculation is a historical gambling game popular in the 18th and 19th centuries, famously depicted in Jane Austen's novels. The game revolves around players buying and selling the right to the 'Highest Trump' currently revealed. It is not trick-taking but a game of chance and negotiation, where the winner is the holder of the highest trump when all cards are revealed.

history.origins: This mild domestic gambling game appeared towards the end of the 18th century and disappeared about a hundred years later. Jane Austen mentions it in Mansfield Park; Dickens in Nicholas Nickleby (1839). Charles Pardon in The Card Player (1868) called it 'without a rival' for Christmas parties. It appears in Cassell's Indoor Amusements (1881) but was omitted from Foster's Complete Hoyle (1897), by which time it was on its way out.
timeline: 1900s: Fades as Poker and Bridge rise.
history.cultural: A game of social dynamics and bluffs.
history.evolution: The negotiation element ('selling the trump') makes it unique among simple card games.

setup.players: Three to nine players; Hoyle (1874) describes it as a round game for several players, with the dealer and each other contributing to the pool.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack, the same as at whist; used with fish or counters on which a value is fixed by the company.
setup.dealing: Ante into a pot. Deal 3 cards face-down to each player. Top card of deck turned for Trump Suit.
setup.equipment: Chips or counters (fish) with agreed value.

rules.objective: Hold the highest trump card revealed at the end of the hand.
rules.gameplay: Everyone antes to a pot. Dealer deals three cards face down to each player in a stack, then turns the next card for trump. If the turn-up is an Ace, the dealer wins the pot immediately. Otherwise the dealer may sell the trump to the highest bidder. In turn from the left of the dealer (or purchaser), each player turns up the top card of their stack; the holder of the current highest trump is exempt and keeps cards concealed. When a higher trump is revealed, that player may sell it. Anyone may also buy face-down cards from another (mystery purchase). When all cards are revealed, the holder of the highest trump wins the pot.
keyRules: Trump is the only suit that counts; highest trump wins the pot.
Dealer turns one card for trump; if Ace, dealer wins immediately.
Dealer may sell the turn-up; players may buy or sell the current highest trump or buy mystery face-down cards.
Players reveal top card of their stack in rotation; holder of current high trump is exempt from revealing.

strategy.basic: Only buy the current High Trump (e.g., King) if many cards are already revealed and the Ace hasn't shown up. The price should reflect the probability of it being beaten. If you hold a face-down card, you can sell it for a mystery price.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Sucker' Bet: Don't buy a Queen of Trumps early in the game. It will likely be beaten. Wait until the Ace/King are accounted for.
strategy.advanced: Market Manipulation: If you hold the High Trump, talk it up. Try to sell it before a better card appears. If you buy, lowball.
tips: The Dealer has a huge advantage on the turn.

variations.name: Five or Jack adds to pot
variations.description: Anyone turning up a Five or a Jack adds one chip to the pot (Irish-style addition).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation only adds a pot penalty rule; no engine constant overrides needed.

variations.name: Spare hand variant
variations.description: A spare hand is dealt and revealed at the end; if it contains a higher trump than the apparent winner's, the pot remains and is added to the next deal.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation adds optional spare-hand resolution; no engine overrides documented in sources.
